acceptance: Scheduled/manual fork workflow performs discovery through deterministic refresh, protected PR merge and verified delivery without commands or fork-write credentials in core.

Scenario proof covers clean refresh, unchanged conflict, human branch/PR collisions, independently modified head, stale head, draft/closed/hold, failed/missing/wrong-publisher checks and partial/repeated reconciliation.
Credential-bearing steps run pinned trusted orchestration only; no candidate code/build/import/hook execution, protection bypass, automatic semantic repair, waiver or patch retirement.

Fork dry-run has no mutations; fork kill switch stops mutations. Actual scoped writer/event behavior is proven and legacy core producer is disabled only after the replacement is ready, with no overlapping active writers.
Ordinary fork review and required checks pass, fork automation PR merges, and deployment/activation evidence is owned by the separate activation task.

description:
Move upstream-facing automation from core scripts/sqlglot_fork_refresh.py and .github/workflows/sqlglot-fork-refresh.yml into BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot. The fork owns scheduled/manual discovery, deterministic patch refresh, its PR lifecycle, protected exact-head merge, required fork CI and verified wheel delivery. Use existing downstream.refresh auto and source/package/engine workflows, not another build/test matrix. Pin trusted orchestration to fork main, separate unprivileged candidate work from fork writer credentials, recover state from existing GitHub refs/PRs/runs, skip unchanged failed inputs until changed or explicit retry, and issue upstream failures in the fork.

Verify prepared output and input identities to establish automation ownership; author/branch names collide with human refreshes and are not authority. Preserve human work, draft/closed/hold state, protection and trusted required checks; protected sha-bound merge with merge method, no bypass/new review App/native-auto-merge setting change. No core pin awareness or core-write credential in fork integration. Prove the fork producer before disabling the old core producer; cutover must leave exactly one upstream writer. Default off until activation. Q19 and core reviewer integration are not fork implementation prerequisites.
